submissions.explanation:
We prove that a single Collatz step strictly decreases every positive even number:

$$n > 0,\ n \text{ even} \quad \Longrightarrow \quad C(n) = \frac{n}{2} < n .$$

Here $C$ is the Collatz step map, $C(n) = n/2$ on even inputs (natural-number division) and $C(n) = 3n+1$ on odd inputs.

The argument is immediate once the branch of the definition is selected. Since $n$ is even, the guard of the conditional in the definition of $C$ evaluates to true, so $C(n)$ reduces to $n / 2$. For a natural number $n \ge 1$ one has $n / 2 < n$, the inequality being strict because $n$ is positive; the case $n = 0$ is genuinely excluded, since $C(0) = 0$.

In Lean the first step is `simp [collatzStep, he]`, which rewrites the goal to $n / 2 < n$, and `omega` closes it, as `omega` handles natural-number division by the literal $2$.

The role of the statement is as the base case of the residue-class decomposition of the Collatz descent principle modulo $4$: the classes $n \equiv 0, 2 \pmod 4$ are exactly the positive even numbers and are settled here in one step, so that only the odd classes remain.
